title: Revenue trend renders a fake ascending "growth" chart while loading and forever on error
detail: `{(trend.data ?? Array.from({length: 12}, (_, i) => ({label: '', heightPct: 6 + i * 7, paise: 0})))}` — when `useRevenueTrend` has no data the panel paints 12 real-looking bars with heights 6%, 13%, 20% … 83%, i.e. a smooth upward revenue curve. There is no `trend.isLoading` / `trend.isError` branch anywhere in the file, and the x-axis label row (line 138) maps over `trend.data ?? []` so it renders nothing. `queryClient` (admin/src/lib/queryClient.ts:7) sets `retry: 1` with no global error handler, so after two failed attempts the query settles in an error state and `trend.data` stays `undefined` permanently.
failure_scenario: A composite index for `orders(status, createdAt)` is missing, or the emulator/network drops one of the 24 aggregate calls fired by `useRevenueTrend`. The admin opens the dashboard and sees a clean 12-month chart trending steadily upward with no error, no spinner and no month labels. Every bar is actually ₹0. Hovering shows the title `₹0`, which reads as a tooltip bug rather than a dead chart. The admin reports revenue growth to the owner from a chart that is pure decoration.
fix: Branch explicitly: render a skeleton/shimmer when `trend.isLoading` and an error row ('Could not load revenue trend — retry') when `trend.isError`. Never synthesize non-zero `heightPct` values. If a placeholder is wanted, use flat/zero-height bars plus the real month labels from `planBuckets(range)` so the axis is present.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. DashboardPage.tsx:129 falls back to a hardcoded 12-bar ascending ramp (heightPct 6,13,20…83, paise 0) rendered with the identical TREND_BAR gradient used for real bars, and the file contains no trend.isLoading/isError branch (trend is referenced only at lines 35, 129, 138) while its sibling panels do handle loading (KPI cards line 66/77/88/95, recent-orders table line 186). The x-axis row at line 138 maps trend.data ?? [], so no labels appear as a cue. The placeholder is provably not equivalent to real empty data: useRevenueTrend (dashboard.ts:451) emits heightPct 2 for zero-revenue buckets, so an empty store renders flat stubs, not a growth curve. The error state is terminal: queryClient.ts sets retry:1 with no global error handler, and grep for throwOnError/ErrorBoundary/useErrorBoundary across admin/src returns zero hits, so a rejection neither surfaces nor is retried and trend.data stays undefined. The failure is reachable because useRevenueTrend fires 2 aggregates per bucket via sumRealisedPaise (dashboard.ts:437-444) and sumTotalPaise/countOrders deliberately re-throw anything other than unimplemented/not-implemented (lines 52-55, 86, 99), so one failing call among the 24 rejects the whole Promise.all. heightPct is used nowhere else except ReportsPage, which renders its trend from real data with no synthetic fallback, so no other surface justifies the placeholder. Not on the already-fixed list (that covers query scoping, not this render fallback) and not on the known-intentional list. Extra symptom: the fallback is always 12 bars even when 30D/7D is selected. Fix is straightforward: add isLoading/isError branches and delete the synthetic array.

title: KPI cards render ₹0 / 0 as real values when the KPI query fails
detail: `const k = kpis.data;` and every card falls back with `?? 0` (lines 65, 76, 87, 94). `kpis.isError` is never read — only `kpis.isLoading` is passed to `KpiCard`, which shows an em-dash. Once react-query exhausts its single retry, `isLoading` flips to false and `isError` to true, so `formatMoneyCompact(0)` → "₹0" and `String(0)` → "0" are painted in the same bold KPI type as genuine numbers. The delta line falls through to the null-baseline branch and shows the neutral 'vs yesterday' / 'across 0 orders' text, which looks like a legitimate quiet day. `useDashboardKpis` fires 21 aggregate queries in one `Promise.all` (dashboard.ts:155-169) — any single rejection (index missing, quota, transient) nukes all four cards at once.
failure_scenario: One of the 21 aggregate queries throws `failed-precondition` (missing index) at 9am. The admin opens the dashboard and sees Today's revenue ₹0, Total orders 0, Pending orders 0 (green 'all clear'), Avg order value ₹0. They conclude the store took no orders and that there is nothing to pack, while real accepted orders sit unpacked in the Orders queue.
fix: Read `kpis.isError` in `DashboardPage` and render an explicit error tile per card (or one banner) with a retry button; never substitute `0` for 'unknown'. Same treatment for `products.error` (the `useLiveCollection` snapshot already carries `error`).

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. DashboardPage.tsx:44 takes `kpis.data` and every KPI card falls back to `?? 0` (lines 65, 76, 87, 94) while only passing `kpis.isLoading` to KpiCard; `isError` is read nowhere in the file, and a grep across admin/src/**/*.tsx finds no `isError` usage at all. The project is on @tanstack/react-query ^5.51.0, where `isLoading = isPending && isFetching`, so once retry:1 is exhausted `isLoading` flips false with `data` still undefined — KpiCard.tsx:20 then paints `value` (formatMoneyCompact(0)="₹0", String(0)="0") in the same 26px extrabold type as real figures, and the pending-orders card shows a green "all clear". There is no safety net: /home/h/barkath/admin/src/lib/queryClient.ts declares no QueryCache onError and no throwOnError, and there is no ErrorBoundary anywhere in admin/src, so a failed KPI fetch is surfaced nowhere. The fan-out count is exact — the Promise.all at dashboard.ts:155-169 has 13 entries but sumRealisedPaise/countRealisedOrders each issue 2 aggregates (lines 118-132) = 21 server aggregates, any one of which rejects the whole promise. Reachability is real, not theoretical: isAggregateUnsupported (dashboard.ts:52-55) deliberately re-throws everything except unimplemented/not-implemented, so failed-precondition (missing status+createdAt index), permission-denied (orders read is isAdmin()-gated in firebase/firestore.rules:69) and resource-exhausted all propagate — and that function's own comment states errors must surface, an intent the UI never completes. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list ("Dashboard queries were scoped" is about query scope) nor KNOWN-INTENTIONAL. Only partial mitigation: the Recent-orders live listener would still list orders under an index/quota failure, giving a contradicting signal; under permission failure both go blank and the display is consistently wrong.

title: Dashboard is reachable by any sub-admin regardless of the `dashboard` module permission, and Firestore rules let them read every order
detail: `{ path: '/', element: <DashboardPage /> }` sits under `RequireAuth` only (admin/src/features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx), which checks that an admin doc exists and nothing else — there is no module guard on any route. `Sidebar.tsx:12` hides nav items whose `modulePermissions[module].view !== true`, so `dashboard` looks gated, but `LoginForm.tsx:41-42` redirects every successful login to `'/'`. On the server side `firebase/firestore.rules:69` allows `read` on `orders/{orderId}` for `isAdmin()` — any sub_admin — with no module check, and `products` (line 51) is world-readable. So the dashboard's revenue aggregates succeed for a sub-admin who has `dashboard.view === false` and `orders.view === false`.
failure_scenario: A super-admin creates a reviews-only moderator with every module unchecked except `reviews`. The moderator logs in, is redirected to `/`, and immediately sees Today's revenue, lifetime Total orders, Average order value, the 12-month revenue trend, the five most recent orders with customer names and totals, and the low-stock list — all data their permission matrix explicitly denies. The Dashboard link is missing from their sidebar, which makes the exposure invisible to the admin who provisioned them.
fix: Add a module-permission route guard (wrap each route element in a `<RequireModule module="dashboard" />`-style component keyed off the same `navConfig` mapping the sidebar uses) and redirect users without `dashboard.view` to their first permitted route after login instead of `'/'`. Optionally tighten the `orders` read rule to `can('orders','view') || can('dashboard','view') || ...` so the client-side gate is backed by rules.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end and could not refute it. (1) admin/src/app/router.tsx wraps every route in RequireAuth -> AppShell only; RequireAuth.tsx checks just `ready` and `admin` truthiness. A grep of all of admin/src for modulePermissions|canView|RequireModule|hasModule finds module checks ONLY in Sidebar.tsx:11-12 (nav visibility) and QuickActions.tsx:42 (button visibility) plus the sub-admin editor — there is no route-level guard component in the codebase. (2) LoginForm.tsx:41-42 sends every cold login to '/', and router.tsx:107 `{path:'*', element:<Navigate to="/" replace/>}` funnels any unknown URL to the dashboard as well, so landing there is unavoidable. (3) 'dashboard' is a real permission module (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:254 MODULE_KEYS, subadmin/api/subadmin.ts:37 label, navConfig.tsx:45 maps '/' to module 'dashboard'), so unchecking it carries a real expectation of enforcement. (4) Server side, firestore.rules isAdmin() is only role()=='super_admin'||'sub_admin' from claims, and `match /orders/{orderId} allow read: if hasAppCheck() && (isOwner(...) || isAdmin())` has no can('orders','view'); the can()/canWrite() helpers are, per their own comment, scoped to direct-write collections, so reads were never module-gated (same for payments, orderRequests, commissions, withdrawalRequests). (5) dashboard/api/dashboard.ts genuinely queries collection(db,'orders') with getAggregateFromServer/sum plus a paged getDocs fallback, and DashboardPage renders useRecentOrders(5) with customer names and totals — these succeed for any sub_admin claim. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (that list covers report/dashboard query scoping and adminModerateReview, which itself confirms reviews-only sub-admins are a provisioned persona) and not on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list. Two minor overstatements that do not sink the claim: the low-stock list derives from `products`, which is world-readable by design and therefore not a leak; and a sub-admin could equally type /orders directly, so the dashboard is the most visible instance of a broader missing-route-guard defect rather than a unique hole. Real, functional, and fixable (module-aware route guard, ideally plus can(module,'view') on the order/payment read rules).

title: Firestore read errors are captured but never rendered — a failed report is shown as a confident all-zero report, and Export CSV happily exports the zeros
detail: `useFetchCollection` does populate `error` on failure (`reports.ts:119-122` — `.catch` sets `{ data: <stale>, loading: false, error }`). `ReportsPage` destructures only `.data` and `.loading` (l.63-68); `orders.error`, `products.error`, `customers.error` and `requests.error` are never referenced anywhere in the file (grep for `\.error` in ReportsPage returns only Tailwind tone strings). Because the catch also sets `loading: false`, the page leaves the loading state and renders `formatMoneyCompact(0)` = '₹0', Orders 0, New customers 0, Refund rate 0%, twelve 2%-high bars and 'No sales data yet'. The Export CSV button is gated only on `loading` (l.101), so it is enabled and writes a report full of zeros to disk. Every other admin screen surfaces failures via toast (e.g. admin/src/features/reviews/routes/ReviewsListPage.tsx:59); Reports swallows them.
failure_scenario: A Firestore rules deploy briefly denies the `customers` collection query (or the network drops mid-fetch). The admin opens Reports, sees 'Total revenue ₹0 / Orders 0 / New customers 0 / Refund rate 0%' with no warning at all, clicks Export CSV, and mails the finance team a report stating the business did zero revenue for the last 12 months. Nothing on screen distinguishes this from a genuinely empty shop.
fix: Surface the union of the four `error` values: render an inline error banner with a Retry that clears `e.started`/re-issues the fetch, and add `|| hasError` to the Export CSV `disabled` prop so a failed snapshot can never be exported.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real, fixable defect. reports.ts:119-122 sets {data: <stale/empty>, loading: false, error} on a failed getDocs; ReportsPage.tsx:63-68 destructures only .data/.loading and never references .error (grep finds only Tailwind `tone === 'error'` strings). Because loading flips to false, KpiStat drops its `—` placeholder and renders formatMoneyCompact(0) = ₹0, Orders 0, New customers 0, Refund rate 0%, twelve 2%-height bars (computeTrend line 355) and 'No sales data yet' — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty shop. Export CSV (line 101) is gated only on `loading`, so it is enabled and downloadReportCsv writes `Total revenue,0.00` to a file. The path is reachable: firestore.rules:157 gates customers/orders/products/orderRequests reads on the isAdmin() custom claim, so an unpropagated token, a rules deploy, or an offline getDocs rejects. No error boundary, unhandledrejection handler, or global toast exists in admin/src to catch it. The codebase's own convention is the opposite: ReturnsListPage.tsx:105-114 renders read errors with the comment 'Read error — surfaced instead of a misleading empty state' and special-cases permission-denied, and BannerListPage:77, SpinnerListPage, CouponsListPage, SubAdminListPage, NotificationsListPage and the settings tabs all consume `error` — useFetchCollection was deliberately given the same CollectionState shape. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Only imprecision: the cited precedent ReviewsListPage.tsx:59 is a mutation toast, not a read-error surface; the real precedent is ReturnsListPage.tsx:105.

title: Category performance silently swaps to lifetime unit counts and presents them under the same "%"
detail: `if (totals.size === 0) { for (const p of products) bump(p.categoryId || p.categorySlug, p.soldCount ?? 0); }` — when the 90-day order aggregation yields nothing, the panel switches metric from 'revenue in paise over 90 days' to 'lifetime units sold from the current product catalogue', with no visual difference in the UI. `totals.size === 0` is true on every first paint (the `categoryOrders` query at line 225 is still in flight while `categoryPerformance` is called synchronously from render at DashboardPage.tsx:46), and stays true forever if that query errors — `categoryOrders.data ?? []` at line 237 swallows the error.
failure_scenario: An admin opens the dashboard. For the first second the bars read 'Perfumes 100%, Dates 62%' from lifetime `soldCount`, then jump to completely different numbers when the order page-walk lands. If the 90-day order read fails (permission, missing index, timeout), the lifetime-units ranking stays on screen indefinitely and the admin makes a merchandising decision from a metric that ignores price, ignores the selected period, and excludes every unpublished product.
fix: Thread the `categoryOrders` query state through instead of the module-level `categorySources` global: render a skeleton while `isLoading`, an error row on `isError`, and a genuine 'No sales in the last 90 days' empty state when the window really is empty. Delete the `soldCount` fallback — it is a different metric.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written (line drift only: the fallback is at dashboard.ts:353-357, not 348). The panel silently swaps metric from '90-day revenue in paise' to 'lifetime units sold from published products' with identical rendering. Verified: (1) DashboardPage.tsx:46 calls categoryPerformance synchronously from render and maps the rows unconditionally at 151-161 — no loading, empty, or error state for the category card, even though useLiveCollection exposes `loading` and it IS used for the recent-orders table at line 186; (2) dashboard.ts:244 does `categoryOrders.data ?? []`, so a failed 90-day order read is indistinguishable from 'no sales' and pins the fallback on screen forever; (3) useLiveCollection (firestoreCache.ts:99-124) returns data:[] while loading, and the products onSnapshot settles before the paged getDocs walk in forEachOrder, so the transient 'products loaded, orders pending' render really does paint soldCount-derived percentages that then jump; (4) the fallback reads products filtered by status=='published' (line 221), so it excludes unpublished SKUs and ignores price and the period — exactly the flaws the function's own doc comment at 303-314 says the soldCount roll-up was replaced for, and the error-swallowing contradicts the file's stated rule at 46-55 ('swallowing it turned a transient outage into a confidently-wrong KPI'). Single caller and single writer of categorySources (grep across admin/src); nothing in web/, app/, or functions/ compensates. Not on the already-fixed list (which covers soldCount increment/decrement only) nor the known-intentional list. Only inaccuracy in the report is the CATEGORY label 'mock-data' — this is real catalogue data used as the wrong metric, not fabricated data.

title: Category performance reads only `order.items`, ignoring legacy orders whose line items live in the subcollection
detail: `for (const it of o.items ?? [])` — the only line-item read. Orders written before the embedded-array migration carry their items solely in `orders/{id}/items`, which the shared type documents explicitly (packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:42-47: "readers must fall back to it when this array is absent") and which the rules still expose (firebase/firestore.rules:71-75). Those orders contribute exactly 0 to every category bucket while still being counted in full by the revenue KPIs and the trend chart (which sum `totalPaise` off the order doc).
failure_scenario: Any pre-migration order inside the 90-day window is invisible to the category split. Immediately after deploy, the dashboard shows Today's revenue ₹4.2L but a Category performance panel built from only the handful of new-format orders — so a category that drove most of the revenue reads near 0%. If every order in the window is legacy, `totals.size === 0` and the panel silently degrades to the `soldCount` fallback described above.
fix: Fall back to `getDocs(collection(db, 'orders', o.id, 'items'))` when `o.items` is absent — or, better, source the split from a server-side rollup (see the perf finding) so the client never has to know about either shape.

verdict.reason: Confirmed: dashboard.ts:348 (`for (const it of o.items ?? [])`) is the only line-item read in categoryPerformance, and nothing upstream hydrates legacy lines. The orders are loaded by the `categoryOrders` queryFn in `useProducts` (dashboard.ts:225-237) as plain order docs; no `orders/{id}/items` read occurs anywhere in the dashboard feature. The legacy subcollection is unambiguously still live: admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:35-45 falls back to it, functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:31-35 falls back to it, web/src/components/account/orders.ts:123,282 falls back to it, firestore.rules:71-75 still exposes it to admins, and no backfill/migration script exists in /home/h/barkath/scripts. OrderItem.category and lineTotalPaise exist, so the aggregation is right for embedded orders and simply blind to legacy ones — those orders still count in full toward the revenue KPIs and trend chart (both sum totalPaise off the order doc), so the panels disagree. CLAUDE.md makes both-path reading an architecture rule whose violation is a defect by definition. Mitigations exist but do not eliminate it: the `totals.size === 0` soldCount fallback only covers the all-legacy case, and normalising to top-category=100% hides rather than fixes skew in a mixed window. Fixability is real — unlike reports.ts:382-387 (which has the same omission but documents it as unavoidable inside a pure function), the dashboard's loader is async and can fetch the subcollection for orders lacking an embedded array. Confidence is medium, not high, only because the identical gap in reports.ts carries an explicit author comment accepting it, suggesting the aggregate surfaces treat this as a known tradeoff; it is not, however, on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists.

title: Week-over-week orders delta compares an 8-day window against a 7-day window
detail: `ordersThisWeek = countOrders([where('createdAt','>=',startOfDay(-7))])` is an open-ended window from midnight 7 days ago to *now*, i.e. 7 full days plus everything so far today = up to 8 calendar days. `ordersPrevWeek` (line 164) is `[startOfDay(-14), startOfDay(-7))` = exactly 7 full days. `pctChange` (line 172) then divides one by the other and the result is surfaced as '▲ X% this week' on the Total orders card (DashboardPage.tsx:81). The same asymmetry exists for the AOV windows at lines 165-168 ([-30, now) = 31 days vs [-60,-30) = 30 days), though the ratio partly cancels there.
failure_scenario: The store takes exactly 100 orders every single day. `ordersThisWeek` = 700 + today's partial (say 50 by midday), `ordersPrevWeek` = 700. The card reports '▲ 7.1% this week' on a perfectly flat business, and the number drifts upward through the day, resetting at midnight. An admin tracking week-on-week growth is reading noise from the window definition.
fix: Make the current window a closed 7 full days — `[startOfDay(-7), startOfDay(0))` — matching the baseline, or compare like-for-like partial windows (last 7 days ending now vs the 7 days ending exactly 7 days ago). Apply the same closure to the 30/60-day AOV windows.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. In /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts, ordersThisWeek is `where('createdAt','>=',startOfDay(-7))` with no upper bound (7 full days + today's elapsed portion), while ordersPrevWeek is the half-open `[startOfDay(-14), startOfDay(-7))` (exactly 7 full days). pctChange divides them and DashboardPage.tsx:81 renders it as '▲ X% this week', so a flat store shows a positive delta that grows through the day and resets at midnight (700+50 vs 700 = +7.1%). No guard, clamp, or server-side recomputation exists; pctChange only null-checks `before > 0`. Not handled elsewhere: ordersWeekDeltaPct appears only in dashboard.ts and DashboardPage.tsx (grep across web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared finds nothing). Not intentional: the interface doc comment in the same file says 'Orders in the last 7 days vs the 7 before that', which the code does not implement, and the sibling analytics screen /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts computeKpis deliberately uses equal-length windows (spanMs mirrored to build prevFrom, comparing [from, now) vs [prevFrom, from)) — so Dashboard and Reports will disagree on the same metric and the correct idiom already exists in-repo. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (that entry covers query scoping and cancelled-order exclusion, which are handled correctly here) nor the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list. Reachable for any store with orders in the prior week. Severity is moderate — misleading KPI, no data corruption — and the AOV pair at lines using -30/-60 shares the asymmetry though the ratio largely cancels it. Fix is a one-liner: add `where('createdAt','<',startOfDay(0))` to the current window (or shift to [-6, now) vs [-13, -6)).

title: Category performance panel has no loading, empty or error state — it renders as a blank box
detail: `{cats.map((c) => …)}` is the entire body of the panel. `categoryPerformance` returns `[]` whenever there are no categories and no products (fresh store, or `useCategories`/`products:published` still loading, or either listener errored — `useLiveCollection` keeps `data: []` and only records the error on the snapshot, which the dashboard never reads). There is no `.length === 0` branch, unlike Recent orders (line 192) and Low stock (line 228) which both have one.
failure_scenario: A brand-new store, or an admin whose `categories` snapshot fails: the right-hand column shows a bordered card containing only the heading 'Category performance' and roughly 200px of empty white. Nothing tells the admin whether it is loading, empty, or broken, so they wait for data that will never arrive.
fix: Add the same treatment the sibling panels already use: a skeleton while `products.loading || categoryOrders.isLoading`, 'Could not load category performance' when either errors, and 'No sales in this period' when the result is genuinely empty.

verdict.reason: Verified accurate. DashboardPage.tsx:151 renders `{cats.map(...)}` as the panel's only body — no loading, empty, or error branch — while the two sibling panels in the same file do have them (recent orders at 186-197, low stock at 228). categoryPerformance (dashboard.ts:308) returns [] when there are no 90-day order line items and no published products; on every initial dashboard render both sources are empty (useLiveCollection seeds data: [] with loading: true, and the categoryOrders react-query starts undefined), so the card is blank until data lands, and permanently blank on a fresh store. The error path is real too: firestoreCache.ts:117-121 keeps data: [] and stores the FirestoreError on the snapshot, and DashboardPage never reads .error; there is no ErrorBoundary anywhere in admin/src and no toast on listener failure, so a denied products/categories snapshot leaves a heading over empty space forever. Because the card is a grid item next to the 180px-tall Revenue trend card with default align-items: stretch, the blank region really is a few hundred px, and the trend card's own placeholder-bar fallback (line 129) makes the neighbour's blankness more conspicuous. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry covers query scoping, not panel states) and not on the known-intentional list. Low severity and UI-only, which is the only reason confidence is medium rather than high, but it is a genuine missing-state gap with a one-line fix.

title: Top products silently ignores legacy orders that keep line items in orders/{id}/items — an explicit architecture-rule violation
detail: `computeTopProducts` iterates only `o.items ?? []` (l.387). The comment on l.385-386 admits it: 'Legacy orders that predate the embedded array keep their lines in the orders/{id}/items subcollection, which a pure function can't read, so they contribute nothing here.' The project rule is that readers must handle BOTH shapes, and the rest of the stack does — `functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:68-74` and `functions/src/returns/requests.ts` both fall back to `orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}`, and the shared type documents the fallback (packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:41-45). Reports is the one reader that skips it, and it skips it without any indication in the UI.
failure_scenario: An order placed before the embedded-items migration is delivered for ₹80,000 inside the reporting window. 'Total revenue' includes the full ₹80,000 (it reads `totalPaise` off the order doc), the revenue-by-month bar includes it, but the products on that order contribute ₹0 to 'Top products'. The two panels on the same screen disagree, and a product that only ever sold on legacy orders never appears in the top-5 no matter how much it sold.
fix: Either fetch the missing lines (collection-group query on `items`, or a per-order subcollection read for orders where `items` is absent, feeding the result into the memoized computation), or — if legacy orders are genuinely gone — remove the dead fallback contract and assert `items` is always present. Silently dropping them while still counting their revenue elsewhere is the defect.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts:387 reads only the embedded `o.items` array, and the in-code comment at lines 382-386 admits legacy subcollection orders contribute nothing. Every other reader in the stack honours the documented dual-shape contract: admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:35-45 (useOrderItems falls back to orders/{id}/items), functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:68-74, web/src/components/account/orders.ts:123 and :282, and packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts states readers must fall back. No server-side aggregate, guard, or alternate source covers Reports; itemsSummary is not used and holds no money. Because revenue KPI and the trend bars read totalPaise off the order doc (reports.ts:253, :348), a legacy order counts fully toward revenue but zero toward Top products, so the two panels on the same screen disagree, and ReportsPage.tsx (157-175) shows no caveat. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Fixable with the existing pattern: hydrate orders missing `items` from their subcollection in useReportOrders before the pure compute. Confidence is medium only because reachability depends on legacy pre-migration orders existing inside the report window (the seed writes embedded items only), not because the code behaviour is in doubt.

title: Top-products revenue uses gross lineTotalPaise while Total revenue uses net totalPaise — the two money definitions do not reconcile
detail: l.391 computes each row as `item.lineTotalPaise ?? quantity * offerPricePaise`. `functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:89` writes `lineTotalPaise: offerPricePaise * l.qty` — the pre-discount line total — and l.624 writes `discountAppliedPaise: 0` unconditionally, so the per-item discount is never allocated. Coupon and spin discounts live only at order level (`discountPaise`), and `totalPaise` is `subtotal - discount + delivery + codSurcharge + tax` (checkout.ts:343-363). So the 'Top products' column, rendered with the same `formatMoneyCompact` and the same gold styling as the revenue KPI, is gross-of-discount money that can exceed the 'Total revenue' figure sitting directly above it. Note the returns CF does the allocation correctly (`functions/src/returns/requests.ts:47-52` pro-rates `orderDiscount` across lines by line total) — reports just doesn't.
failure_scenario: A campaign runs a 60%-off coupon. In a month with ₹4,00,000 of realised revenue, the admin sees Top products listing five items summing to ₹9,50,000 — more than double the 'Total revenue' KPI on the same screen — and exports both numbers into the same CSV under headings that both say 'Revenue (INR)'.
fix: Pro-rate the order-level `discountPaise` (and `spinRewardPaise`) across lines by line-total share, exactly as `functions/src/returns/requests.ts:47-52` already does, before accumulating into `acc`; or relabel the column 'Gross sales' so it is not read as revenue.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts:391 sums item.lineTotalPaise, which functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:109 writes as offerPricePaise * qty (pre-discount), with checkout.ts:703 hardcoding discountAppliedPaise: 0 on every embedded item; that is the only code path writing orders.items, and no other surface (web/, app/, functions/, seed) ever populates a per-item discount. Meanwhile reports.ts:252-253 computes Total revenue from o.totalPaise, which is net of discountPaise. So Top products is gross-of-discount money rendered with the same formatMoneyCompact styling on the same screen (ReportsPage.tsx:191) and exported under a numeric 'Revenue (INR)' CSV column (reports.ts:440-443) alongside the net KPI. Decisively, the repo already contains the correct allocation and documents why the gross figure is wrong: functions/src/returns/requests.ts:89-102 pro-rates orderDiscount across lines by line total (refundAmountPaise = lineTotal - discountShare) — so this is an internal inconsistency with an in-repo precedent, not a deliberate GMV metric. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists; the path runs on every Reports render; the fix is well-defined and uses data already on the order doc. Caveats that do not change the verdict: the claimed magnitude is exaggerated (needs a ~60% blanket discount, and the two numbers never reconcile exactly anyway since top-5 is a subset and totalPaise includes delivery/tax/COD surcharge), and the returns citation should be requests.ts:89-102, not 47-52. Scope note: the identical gross aggregation exists at admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts:364 (categoryPerformance), so a fix should cover both.

title: The date-range subtitle prints the end date's year for both ends, so the 12M/30D labels state a wrong start date — and that wrong label is written into the CSV
detail: `rangeLabel` (l.47-52) formats `from` and `to` with `{ day:'numeric', month:'short' }` — year deliberately omitted — then appends a single `to.getFullYear()`. Whenever the window crosses a year boundary (always, for 12M) the start date is captioned with the wrong year. It is rendered as the page subtitle (ReportsPage.tsx:94) and embedded verbatim in the export header (`Range,${range} (${rangeLabel(range)})`, reports.ts:427).
failure_scenario: On 23 Jul 2026 with the default 12M preset, `rangeStart` returns 1 Aug 2025 but the header reads '1 Aug – 23 Jul 2026'. An admin reading it left-to-right sees a range starting in August 2026 — i.e. the future — or assumes the report covers Aug 2026 to Jul 2026. Selecting 30D on 5 Jan 2026 gives '7 Dec – 5 Jan 2026' when the window actually starts 7 Dec 2025. The exported CSV carries the same wrong range string, so the misstatement survives into any spreadsheet built on it.
fix: Include the year on the start date whenever `from.getFullYear() !== to.getFullYear()`: e.g. `${day(from)}${sameYear ? '' : ' ' + from.getFullYear()} – ${day(to)} ${to.getFullYear()}`.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly by executing the real rangeStart/rangeLabel logic: on 23 Jul 2026 the default 12M preset yields the label "1 Aug – 23 Jul 2026" while the window actually starts 1 Aug 2025; 30D on 5 Jan 2026 yields "7 Dec – 5 Jan 2026" for a window starting 7 Dec 2025. Both of the claim's scenarios match character-for-character. Refutation attempts all failed: rangeLabel has only two call sites (ReportsPage.tsx:94 subtitle and reports.ts:427 CSV header) with no guard, wrapper or alternate date row — that string is the CSV's only statement of the period; the path is reachable on every visit since ReportsPage defaults to '12M'; it is not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and the JSDoc's same-year example ("1 Jan – 16 Jul 2026") shows the cross-year case was overlooked rather than deliberate. It is display-only — the analytics window itself is computed correctly — but a wrong start-date year printed as the report period and embedded in the exported CSV is incorrect information, not styling. One caveat: the claim's "always, for 12M" is slightly overstated, since in December the 12M window starts 1 Jan of the same year and the label is correct; that does not change the substance. Fix is a one-liner: append the year to `from` when from.getFullYear() !== to.getFullYear(). Confidence is medium only because the impact is confined to a label/export string with no effect on computed figures.
